u p i ternary system

Chat date: Sep 17 · Original chat on grok.com ↗ · Raw capture (.md)

Speculative / personal construction

Speculative / personal construction. Turn 1 is ordinary base 3 with renamed digits; the later u/p/i mapping is Joshua's own construction, not a standard numeral system.
Capture note. A custom base-3 numeral system (digits u, p, i) and its conversion to binary. Kept as numeration-system math; the later turns are converter code.

Joshua's messages (verbatim)

  1. Using u p and I create a 3 letter system like binary but with the letters u p and i
  2. I mean p means 1 u means I and so u is 0 not in binary nut no value
  3. make a converter for binary to this system

Grok's response (as captured)

Turn 1: base-3 system

A 3-symbol system like binary is base 3. Binary uses {0,1}\{0, 1\}{0,1}; this uses {u,p,i}\{u, p, i\}{u,p,i}.

Digit values: u=0u = 0u=0, p=1p = 1p=1, i=2i = 2i=2.

Place values are powers of 3, right to left: 30,31,32,33,…3^0, 3^1, 3^2, 3^3, \ldots30,31,32,33,…

decimal UPI
0 u
1 p
2 i
3 pu
4 pp
5 pi
6 iu
7 ip
8 ii
9 puu
13 ppp
26 iii
27 puuu

Example: pui\text{pui}pui =p⋅9+u⋅3+i⋅1=1⋅9+0⋅3+2⋅1=11= p \cdot 9 + u \cdot 3 + i \cdot 1 = 1 \cdot 9 + 0 \cdot 3 + 2 \cdot 1 = 11=p⋅9+u⋅3+i⋅1=1⋅9+0⋅3+2⋅1=11.

Converter in artifacts/upi_ternary.py: int_to_upi(n) (decimal to UPI string) and upi_to_int(s) (UPI string to decimal).

Turn 2: revised mapping

Mapping updated: p=1p = 1p=1 (the only unit that counts), uuu = no value (blank, not a binary-style 0), iii = "I" mark (third letter, not a place-value 2).

string p (ones) i (I marks) u (blanks) value
p 1 0 0 1
ppp 3 0 0 3
u 0 0 1 none
i 0 1 0 I
upi 1 1 1 1 + I
uuppi 2 1 2 2 + I

So uuppi has value 2 (not a base-3 number). Grok noted: read("uuppi") gives ones=2, marks_I=1, blanks=2, value=2; write(ones=3, marks_I=1, blanks=2) gives uuippp.

Turn 3: binary converter

Map: binary 1 → p; binary 0 → u (written but no value); i is an optional I-mark, not a bit.

dec binary UPI
0 0 u
1 1 p
2 10 pu
5 101 pup
8 1000 puuu
13 1101 ppup

Count mode: 5 (101) → ppppp; 13 (1101) → 13 × p.

Usage (from upi_ternary.py):

from upi_ternary import bin_to_upi, upi_to_bin, upi_to_int

bin_to_upi(13)              # 'ppup'
bin_to_upi("1101")          # 'ppup'
bin_to_upi(13, "count")     # 'ppppppppppppp'
bin_to_upi(13, mark_I=1)    # 'ippup'

upi_to_bin("ppup")          # '1101'
upi_to_int("ppup")          # 13

Grok noted that i is dropped when converting back to binary.
